values.name: MaxWidestLane
values.tooltip: Aggregate: max widest-lane across all roads, applied uniformly to the polygon.

values.name: MaxHalfProfile
values.tooltip: Aggregate: max half-profile across all roads, applied uniformly to the polygon.

values.name: ConvexFit
values.tooltip: Per-road radius geometrically fitted to clear neighboring roads' profile strips.

values.name: None
values.tooltip: No connection restrictions.

values.name: Raw
values.tooltip: Read int32 attribute from edges, interpret directly as EZoneShapeLaneConnectionRestrictions bitmask.

values.name: ValueMap
values.tooltip: Read int32 attribute from edges, look up in TMap to get bitmask.

values.name: All
values.tooltip: A seam must pass every enabled geometric guard.

values.name: Any
values.tooltip: A seam passes if at least one enabled geometric guard passes.

values.name: Equal
values.tooltip: Adjacent merge-group ids must be strictly equal.

values.name: NotEqual
values.tooltip: Adjacent merge-group ids must differ.

values.name: Near
values.tooltip: Adjacent merge-group ids must be within Tolerance of each other.

values.name: NotNear

values.name: SortDirection
values.tooltip: Use the Direction Settings sorting rules to determine road orientation.

values.name: DepthFirst
values.tooltip: Deprecated alias for Traffic Flow -- kept for backward compatibility with saved assets.

values.name: GlobalDirection
values.tooltip: Orient all roads to flow along a global direction vector.

values.name: TrafficFlow
values.tooltip: Propagate orientation from leaf nodes inward. Produces consistent lane direction at intersections and along loops. Isolated loops use the Orientation Direction vector as a CW/CCW hint.

values.name: Replace
values.tooltip: Auto value replaces the manual/attribute radius.

values.name: Min
values.tooltip: radius = max(manual, auto). Auto acts as a floor.

values.name: Max
values.tooltip: radius = min(manual, auto). Auto acts as a ceiling.

values.name: Offset
values.tooltip: radius = auto + manual. Manual is a uniform additive buffer.

values.name: Default
values.tooltip: Don't set tangent length -- ZoneGraph handles it.

values.name: Manual
values.tooltip: Use a constant or per-point attribute value.

values.name: Auto
values.tooltip: Average distance to chain neighbors, divided by 3.

values.name: CatmullRom
values.tooltip: |P_next - P_prev| * 0.5.

values.name: PerProfile
values.tooltip: One attribute set per lane profile. Rows are lanes; profile-level values are written to the @Data domain, matching the metadata on Cluster to Zone Graph path outputs.

values.name: Merged
values.tooltip: A single attribute set with one row per lane across all profiles; profile-level values are repeated as regular columns.

UPCGExClusterToZoneGraphSettings.name: Cluster to Zone Graph
UPCGExClusterToZoneGraphSettings.purpose: Turns a cluster into Zone Graph data the engine's navigation can use. A cluster already says which points connect; what Zone Graph wants is lanes with direction, profiles and tags, and this is the translation between the two. It is the bridge node of the plugin, and everything else in the book leads to it.
UPCGExClusterToZoneGraphSettings.situation: A road, path or corridor network built as a cluster that now has to exist as navigable Zone Graph.

mechanism.text: Every edge becomes a lane and every Vtx becomes a point where lanes meet. `Direction Settings` decide which way each lane runs, which Zone Graph needs and a cluster does not carry: an edge joins two Vtx without preferring an end. The polygon and road settings decide what each lane is made of, and merging can join lanes that continue through a junction so a straight run does not become a chain of stubs.

DirectionSettings.tooltip: Defines the direction in which points will be ordered to form the final paths.
DirectionSettings.semantics: Where each lane's direction comes from, and the setting with no equivalent on the cluster side. A cluster's edges are undirected, so this is doing more than reading a property: it is deciding something the source data never expressed.

OrientationMode.tooltip: How road orientation is determined. Affects lane profile alignment at intersections.
OrientationMode.semantics: How a lane's cross-section is turned about its own length, which decides which way is up on sloped or banked runs. It is separate from the lane's direction, so a lane can run the right way and still be rolled the wrong way.

OrientationDirection.tooltip: Global direction vector used to orient roads. In GlobalDirection mode, each road aligns with this vector. In TrafficFlow mode, used as a CW/CCW hint for isolated loops with no leaf connections.

bEnableFlipFilters.tooltip: Enable the use of filters to define whether a road direction should be flipped or not (reversing the auto-computed direction).

fields.name: PolygonRadiusAttribute
fields.tooltip: Per-point polygon radius override. Read from: Points. Attribute type: double.

fields.name: AutoRadiusMode
fields.tooltip: Auto-compute polygon radius from connected road lane profiles.

fields.name: AutoRadiusPolicy
fields.tooltip: How the auto-computed value combines with the manual / attribute polygon radius.

fields.name: ConvexFitSettings
fields.tooltip: Convex Fit refinement parameters (acute-angle clamp and fallback for unconstrained roads).

fields.name: PolygonRoutingTypeAttribute
fields.tooltip: Per-point polygon routing override. Read from: Points. Attribute type: int32. Values: 0=Bezier, 1=Arcs.

fields.name: PolygonPointTypeAttribute
fields.tooltip: Per-point polygon shape point type override. Read from: Points. Attribute type: int32. Values: 0=Sharp, 1=Bezier, 2=AutoBezier, 3=LaneProfile.

fields.name: AdditionalIntersectionTags
fields.tooltip: Default intersection tags applied to all polygons.

fields.name: IntersectionTagsMode
fields.tooltip: How additional intersection tags are sourced from attributes.

fields.name: IntersectionTagsAttribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name for intersection tag values. Read from: Points. Attribute type: int32.

fields.name: IntersectionTagsValueMap
fields.tooltip: Maps integer attribute values to intersection tag masks.

fields.name: InnerTurnRadiusPrimary
fields.tooltip: Inner turn radius for polygon arc routing. Read from: Edges (nearest edge to polygon connection).

fields.name: InnerTurnRadiusSecondary
fields.tooltip: Separate inner turn radius for the end polygon connection. When disabled, Primary value is used for both.

fields.name: RollPrimary
fields.tooltip: Roll angle (degrees) applied to polygon connection points. Read from: Edges (nearest edge to polygon connection).

fields.name: RollSecondary
fields.tooltip: Separate roll for the end polygon connection. When disabled, Primary value is used for both.

fields.name: ConnectionRestrictionMode
fields.tooltip: How lane connection restrictions are sourced.

fields.name: ConnectionRestrictionsAttribute
fields.tooltip: Attribute name for connection restriction values. Read from: Edges.

fields.name: ConnectionRestrictionsValueMap
fields.tooltip: Maps integer attribute values to connection restriction flags.

fields.name: RoadPointTypeAttribute
fields.tooltip: Per-edge road shape point type override. Read from: Points. Attribute type: int32. Values: 0=Sharp, 1=Bezier, 2=AutoBezier, 3=LaneProfile.

fields.name: RoadTangentLengthMode
fields.tooltip: How road tangent lengths are determined. Controls bezier curve tightness.

fields.name: TangentLength
fields.tooltip: Tangent length value -- constant or per-point attribute.

fields.name: TangentLengthScale
fields.tooltip: Scale multiplier applied to all tangent lengths (manual or computed).

fields.name: bClampTangentLengthToShortNeighbor
fields.tooltip: When enabled (Auto/CatmullRom only), clamp the computed tangent length so it never exceeds 1/3 of the shorter neighbor segment. Prevents bezier control overshoot at points adjacent to polygon-boundary crossings, where one neighbor is the short trim segment and the other is a long road segment. Leave disabled to keep the original averaged-length behavior.

fields.name: EndpointTrimBuffer
fields.tooltip: After trimming, remove road points closer than this distance to the polygon boundary.

fields.name: LaneProfileAttribute
fields.tooltip: Lane profile override. Read from: Edges (majority vote). Attribute type: FName. Must match a registered lane profile name in ZoneGraph settings.

MergeSettings.tooltip: Merge adjacent polygons that pass the Merge Conditions filter. Fuses two polygons joined by a single road into one, dissolving the road between them.

fields.name: MergeGroupAttribute
fields.tooltip: Per-node int32 merge-group id. 0 = never merge (either endpoint). How two adjacent non-zero ids must relate is set by Match. Read from: Points (vtx).

fields.name: MergeGroupMatch
fields.tooltip: How the two adjacent group ids must relate for the pair to merge.

fields.name: MergeGroupTolerance
fields.tooltip: Tolerance (in id units) for the ~= / !~= group match.

fields.name: GuardCombine
fields.tooltip: How the enabled geometric guards combine when deciding whether a seam may contract.

fields.name: MaxFaceGap
fields.tooltip: Guard: signed gap between the two facing connection faces (uu) must be at or below this. Positive = road remains between them; 0 = touching; negative = require overlap.

fields.name: MaxSeamAngle
fields.tooltip: Guard: the two arms must be near-collinear -- their misalignment angle (degrees) must be at or below this. 0 = perfectly inline.

fields.name: bGuardSingleEdge
fields.tooltip: Guard: only contract single-edge seams (the road between the two polygons is one cluster edge, with no pass-through nodes).

fields.name: MaxArms
fields.tooltip: Guard: only contract when both polygon nodes have at most this many OTHER arms -- cluster degree excluding the road being merged away. Prevents dissolving busy junctions.

MergeSettings.semantics: How lanes passing through a junction without branching are joined, while merging is enabled above. Without merging every edge becomes its own lane, which is correct and produces far more lanes than the geometry needs.

bOutputPolygonPaths.tooltip: Output polygon shapes as closed PCG paths.

bOutputRoadPaths.tooltip: Output road splines as PCG paths with tangent attributes.

ArriveName.tooltip: Name of the 'FVector' attribute the incoming tangent is written to on each road path point.

LeaveName.tooltip: Name of the 'FVector' attribute the outgoing tangent is written to on each road path point.

PostProcessFunctionNames.tooltip: Specify a list of functions to be called on the target actor after dynamic mesh creation. Functions need to be parameter-less and with "CallInEditor" flag enabled.

hints.text: Lanes are directional and cluster edges are not, so this is where a one-way network is decided. A network meant to run both ways needs that expressed here rather than assumed from the cluster.

UPCGExGetZoneGraphConstantsSettings.name: Get Zone Graph Constants
UPCGExGetZoneGraphConstantsSettings.purpose: Lists what the project's Zone Graph settings actually define, as data. Lane profiles and tags are configured in project settings and referenced by name everywhere else, so a graph that has to pick one is otherwise typing a string and hoping. This makes the real list available to be read, matched against or picked from.
UPCGExGetZoneGraphConstantsSettings.situation: A graph choosing a lane profile or tag, where the names should come from the project rather than being typed.

mechanism.text: The project's Zone Graph settings are read and emitted as attribute sets, with `Mode` deciding whether that is the profiles or the tags. The result is data rather than configuration, so it can be filtered, matched or picked from like anything else. Nothing is written back: this reads the project settings and never changes them.

Mode.tooltip: How lane profile data is laid out across output attribute sets.
Mode.semantics: Which of the two lists is emitted. They are separate outputs rather than one combined set, so a graph needing both places two of these nodes.

hints.text: The values come from project settings, so what this node emits changes when the project changes rather than when the graph does. A graph matching against a hard-coded name will silently stop matching if the project renames it; matching against this output will not.
